assessment: This fundamental study provides compelling evidence for dysgranular insular involvement in top-down and bottom-up interoceptive processing by building on previous evidence using state-of-the-art methods. Its translational application in ADE patients corroborates the assumption that the mid-insula may indeed be a locus of 'interoceptive disruption' in psychiatric disorders, which underscores the study's high relevance for both body-brain as well as clinical research.
